key_insight: RedSage creates a cybersecurity-focused generalist LLM by continual pretraining on a curated 11.8B-token corpus, delivering domain-aware capabilities without relying on proprietary APIs. This bridges the gap between privacy risks of hosted services and the poor domain fit of untuned open models.
problem_solved: Security teams need a privacy-preserving, domain-adapted assistant that supports diverse cybersecurity workflows; existing solutions either expose sensitive data to proprietary APIs or use open models that lack specialized cybersecurity knowledge.
method: Curate a large cybersecurity corpus (11.8B tokens, 28.6K documents) via large-scale web filtering plus manual collection covering frameworks, offensive techniques, and security tools.
Perform continual pretraining of a foundation LLM on the curated dataset to produce a domain-adapted cybersecurity generalist (RedSage).
Design the model and deployment workflow to support diverse security operations while minimizing exposure of sensitive data (privacy-aware integration).
impact: Provides AI/ML and security practitioners a practical path to deploy high-quality, domain-tuned assistants that improve performance on infosec tasks and reduce dependence on proprietary, privacy-risky APIs.
visual_elements: Dataset composition pie/chart: tokens, doc counts, and topic breakdown (frameworks, offensive techniques, tools).
Pipeline diagram: data curation → continual pretraining → RedSage model → privacy-aware deployment.
Before/after comparison bar chart: baseline open model vs. RedSage on representative cybersecurity tasks.
Icon set: shield (privacy), gear (tools/workflows), book (knowledge corpus), network/alert (SOC use cases).
paper_authors: Naufal Suryanto, Muzammal Naseer, Pengfei Li, Syed Talal Wasim, Jinhui Yi
